rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarīm means wholly cut or severed; it can describe cut fruit, a harvested field, a night portion, or barren sand.
rows.anchor: tamamen kesilmiş veya kesik demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted interpretation takes the orchard itself, rather than only its fruit, as cut from the roots and burned black like ash.
rows.anchor: o bağın meyvesinin değil, kendisinin kökünden kesilip yanmış, kül gibi karara kalmış olduğu mervîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sworn plan came true, but to their harm and in an unforeseen way, not as they intended or by their own hand.
rows.anchor: Demek ki yemin ettikleri fiil olmuştu, fakat gönüllerindeki gibi ve kendi elleriyle lehlerine değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it their own cultivation assumes sole ownership; عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ evokes attacking and cutting it down as if striking an enemy.
rows.anchor: yalnız kendileri yetiştirmiş, sade kendilerinin ekimi, kültürü imiş gibi حَرْثُكُمْ diyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They meant to finish the harvest completely and leave nothing for anyone, acting with extreme greed.
rows.anchor: onu ekin biçer gibi kesip bitirmek niyetiyle düşmanın üzerine saldırır gibi kıymak azmiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They forgot that the previous day they had needed oaths to reassure each other and establish their company; the orchard's yield would likewise depend on trust.
rows.anchor: dün birbirleriyle mukavele ederlerken birbirlerini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should have remembered that God gave them the orchard and watched over it while they slept, and that God and needy servants had rights in it.
rows.anchor: o bağ ve hars kendilerinden evvel onu kendilerine veren ve onlar uyurken onu gözetecek olan Allah’ındır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude required generosity toward the poor, sharing some means from the crop, and cultivating beneficiaries and well-wishers instead of enemies through greed and despotism.
rows.anchor: öyle istibdad ile hareket etmeyip mümkin olabildiği kadar onlardan bazılarını da sebeplendirmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rushed out without considering the orchard's condition and whispered their exclusion of the poor so no one would hear.
rows.anchor: bunu da kimse işitmesin diye seslerini dahi kıskanır bir surette fısıl fısıl, mızır mızır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥard is read as forceful prevention and despotism: they set out early with power only for greed and anger.
rows.anchor: yani hızlı bir men‘ü istibdâda, mücerred bir hırs u gazaba güçleri yeterek erkenden gittiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collective speed and despotism can be more powerful and dreadful than an individual's.
rows.anchor: Demek ki cemiyetin hızı ve istibdâdı ferdden daha kuvvetli ve daha fecî‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They first thought they had lost their way, then recognized punishment and deprivation greater than what they had planned for the poor, and despaired of present and future.
rows.anchor: evvelâ yalnız dalâletlerine hükmettiler, sonra da cezâya uğradıklarına, men‘etmek istedikleri miskinden ziyade mahrum bırakıldıklarına hükmettiler

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas, Mücâhid, Katâde ve Dahhâk
rows.claim: As cited by Ibn Jarir, they explain wasat in 2:143 as just; awsatuhum is its superlative, meaning the most just, discerning, good, and moderate, not middle-aged or numerically central.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in İbn Abbas’tan ve Mücâhid’den ve Katâde’den ve Dahhâk’ten rivayet ederek tasrih ettiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moderate man was a wise, just individual whose worth the group had initially failed to recognize or heed.
rows.anchor: bir cemiyet içinde bidâyeten kadri takdir edilmemiş, söylediği dinlenmemiş bir ferdin kıymetini gösterir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither extreme individualism nor collectivism is right: the individual appears in society and society stands through individuals, while both depend on God.
rows.anchor: ne yalnız infiradda ne de ferde hiç kıymet vermek istemeyen müfrit ictimâ‘iyatçıların zannettikleri gibi yalnız cemiyettedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their covenant formed by relying on God's unity, but they failed because they disregarded God's rights in their agreement and conduct.
rows.anchor: ferdler Hakk’ın birliğine istinad ile bir mukavele yapmadan cemiyet yapamadılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ here means acknowledging God's transcendence and sovereignty, rejecting injustice and domination, observing rights, and making an exception rather than acting despotically.
rows.anchor: Hak teâlâ’nın nezâhetini tanısanız, O’nun noksandan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke is not merely wounded pride about being ignored; it calls them out of despair and guards against the greater sin of accusing God of injustice.
rows.anchor: bu kere düştükleri yeisten kurtarmak ve yeisle Allah’a zulüm isnad etmek gibi Allah’a karşı daha büyük bir küfr ü günaha düşmekten sakındırmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exalt God and admit that their thoughtless oath, omission of an exception, and resolve to neglect the poor wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: Allah’ı tenzih ve kendi zâlimliklerini, düşüncesiz yemin, istisnâyı terk ve fukarâya bakmamaya azmetmekle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mutual reproaches begin repentance: each discusses excess and deficiency, criticizes personal faults, and explains regret to the others.
rows.anchor: ben şu kusuru ettim, sen şöyle yaptın

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: The commentary says some beautified and encouraged the wrong, some accepted it, some warned against it, some disobeyed the leader, and some silently consented.
rows.anchor: kimi ettikleri zulmü tezyin ve teşvik etmiş, kimisi onu kabul etmiş, kimisi sakınılmasını emretmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They declare themselves transgressors deserving punishment and locate the fault in themselves, rather than in their Lord.
rows.anchor: bizler hakikaten azgınlarmışız cezâya müstahik imişiz, bütün kusur bizim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hope God may replace the lost worldly garden with something better, chiefly the afterlife's blissful garden free of grief and affliction; worldly good can be its prelude.
rows.anchor: o asıl âhiret ecri, öyle gussadan, belâdan âzâde olan na‘îm cennetidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their final repentance seeks God alone and His pleasure, leaving whether He grants their request to Him; even this wish is not treated as sufficient until all desire is directed to God.
rows.anchor: bütün rağbetimizi münhasıran O’na çevirdik, O’na O’nun rızâsına ermek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment awakens those able to understand, returns them to the truth, and protects them from greater danger while opening a path to greater good.
rows.anchor: azab bilenleri, bilmek anlamak kābiliyetinde olanları böyle dünyada uyandırır, yola getirir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife punishment is greater, eternal, and concerns life rather than property; its warning helps only before it occurs, through revelation, faith, and analogy from worldly punishments.
rows.anchor: âhiret azâbı daha büyüktür. Mala değil canadır. Geçici değil ebedîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly punishment can teach through experience after it occurs, but the final afterlife punishment cannot be learned from by experience and must be known beforehand.
rows.anchor: Lâkin âhiret azâbı sondur, o tecribeye gelmez, artık bütün tecribeler onda tükenmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If deniers who call the revelations old tales learned from worldly punishment as the orchard owners learned from their moderate companion, they would believe and seek protection from the greater punishment.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’in tebliğ ettiği âyetleri dinlerler

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: Asked about the orchard owners' later fate, Qatada says it is a difficult question because the verse does not state it and it belongs to the unseen.
rows.anchor: zor bir şey teklif ettin” demiş, yani

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid is reported to say that the owners repented and God gave them something better.
rows.anchor: Allah da kendilerine daha hayırlısını verdi” diye menkuldür

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says it reached him that they became sincere, God rewarded their sincerity with a garden called al-Ḥayawān, whose grape cluster a mule could carry.
rows.anchor: Bana böyle bâliğ oldu ki onlar ihlâs ettiler, Allah teâlâ da onların sıdkına mükâfat buyurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥayawān denotes the true life of the afterlife, as in 29:64, so the report means they received the eternal garden; their good ending explains the definite expression owners of the garden.
rows.anchor: mahz-ı hayat demek olan “el-hayevân” dâr-ı âhiretin ismi olduğu anlaşılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the orchard owners' story ends with turning toward God, the following verse also points to their eventual fate.
rows.anchor: Madem ki onların sonu ancak Allah’a rağbetle neticelendirilmiştir, o hâlde şu gelen âyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhl may mean oil dregs or metal melted in a crucible; the image is boiling and displaying varied colors.
rows.anchor: Mühl gibi “mühl” yağ tortusu, yahut potada eritilen maden gibi kaynar, türlü renkler arzeder

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Ibn Masud is reported to gloss muhl as molten silver of changing colors.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan “eritilen gümüş gibi mütelevvin” diye rivayet edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihn is wool, especially wool dyed in many colors; mountains likewise have varied colors.
rows.anchor: Yün, bâhusus türlü renklere boyanmış olan elvan yün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are shown to one another amid such terror that they cannot ask each other's condition, let alone search farther away.
rows.anchor: öyle bir dehşet ki birbirlerine gösterilip dururlarken bile soramaz, nerede kaldı ki uzağı arasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faṣīla means the people, tribe, clan, or community that raised, sheltered, and embraced a person when in need.
rows.anchor: içlerinde yetiştiği ve başı sıkıldığı zaman kendisini kucaklayan, barındıran kavm ü kabilesini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lazā is a name for Hell, a blazing and engulfing fire.
rows.anchor: alevli salgın ateş cehennemin bir ismi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazzāʿatan is construed either as a circumstantial accusative from Lazā or as an accusative of specification with an implied subject; when read nominative it is a predicate after a predicate or an adjective.
rows.anchor: “Nüzû‘”dan saldırıcı, “nez‘”den, soyucu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shawāʾ means limbs such as hands and feet, or the plural of the scalp's skin; the fire strips them, with skin replaced so torment continues.
rows.anchor: “Şevâ” el ayak gibi etrâf; nitekim avcı kol, bacak gibi öldürmeyecek noktadan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Halūʿ expresses a vague bad temperament between haste, impatience, whining, intensity, and greed; the next verses explain it.
rows.anchor: “Helû‘”, esasında bir çabukluk mânası bulunan bir taraftan tahammülsüzlük, mızıkçılık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When pain, hardship, poverty, or illness touches a person, he complains, writhes, cries out, cannot endure it, and seeks help from others.
rows.anchor: kendisine meselâ bir ağrı, bir sıkıntı, bir yoksulluk, hastalık gibi bir acı dokundu mu kıvranır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When wealth, health, or status comes, the person becomes greedy and withholding, quickly forgets earlier distress, blocks good, and hoards what he gets.
rows.anchor: bir servete, bir sıhhate, bir mansıba kondu mu hırsından, kıskançlığından kimseye bir şey vermek istemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The engulfing fire calls this person because he turns away from right and good, accumulates possessions, and stores them up.
rows.anchor: Eline geçeni toplayıp yığmaya, saklamaya çalışır. Onun için de o salgın ateş onu çağırır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing people who pray are exempt from this bad character, torment, and evil end, and are honored in gardens through the virtues that follow.
rows.anchor: o mü’min musallîler, o huydan, o ahlâksızlıktan, o azabdan, o kötü âkıbetten müstesnâdırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first virtue is keeping up prayer consistently, not merely believing it obligatory but performing the known prayers without abandoning them and remembering God and His commands.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın emrettiği ve Peygamber’in tâlim buyurduğu vechile mâlum olan namazlarını terketmeksizin devam üzere kılmayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wealth contains a fixed, obligatory right proportionate to their means, not merely voluntary aid, given willingly to both petitioners and deprived people too proud to ask.
rows.anchor: malına göre muayyen bir nisbette mâlum bir hak, edâsı farz bir Allah borcu olmak üzere bir vergi vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They affirm the Day of Judgment, resurrection, and accounting, and demonstrate sincerity through bodily and financial obedience, not merely theoretical assent.
rows.anchor: “tasdîk”ten murad yalnız kalben veya lisânen tasdîk-i nazarîden ibaret olmayıp ona sadakati bi’l-amel fiilen isbat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fear God's punishment because they may have failed duties or committed what is forbidden; they do not rely on their deeds and regard them as small before God.
rows.anchor: Vazifelerinde, vecîbelerinde kusur etmiş veya menhî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is assured against the Lord's punishment: people cannot claim to have fulfilled every duty and avoided every danger, and only God knows what tomorrow holds.
rows.anchor: insan için bu dünyada her şeyi halletmiş, bütün vecîbelerini îfâ ve bütün mahzurlardan ictinab eylemiş bulunduğunu iddia etmek kābil olamadığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guarding one's sexual parts means not exposing them; lawful spouses and owned female slaves are exceptions and incur no blame because marriage or ownership makes relations lawful.
rows.anchor: ırzlarını, apışlarını korurlar, kimseye açmazlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone, male or female, seeking sexual pleasure beyond spouses and owned women turns to unlawful sex and is a transgressor deserving censure and restraint.
rows.anchor: nikâhlı eşlerinin ve milk cariyelerinin mâverâsında zevk arayan, ırzlarını korumayan, harama açılan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trusts and covenants cover words, states, actions, property, God's and people's rights, and duties to family, neighbors, and others; every divine gift is also a trust not to be misused.
rows.anchor: Kavilden, hâlden, fiilden, maldan, hukūkullahdan, hukūk-ı ibâddan kendilerine emanet edilen şeylere

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: A report in Bukhari and Muslim says four traits mark a pure hypocrite, while possessing one marks a trait of hypocrisy: betraying trust, lying, breaking promises, and acting obscenely in disputes.
rows.anchor: dört haslet kendisinde bulunan hâlis münafık olur. O dörtten birisi bulunan da kendisinde nifaktan bir haslet

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: In a sermon reported by Bayhaqi from Anas, the Prophet says that one without trust has no faith and one without a covenant has no religion.
rows.anchor: haberiniz olsun ki emaneti olmayan kimsenin imanı yoktur, ahdi olmayan kimsenin dini yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They stand by testimony truthfully and justly, without concealing any part or distorting it; it is singled out for emphasis despite belonging under trusts.
rows.anchor: Bu, “emânât”ta dâhil olmakla beraber ehemmiyetini beyan için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's continuation means never abandoning it and observing its times; guarding it means careful attention to its prior, concurrent, and subsequent conditions.
rows.anchor: “devam” hiçbir vakit terkedilmemesi için evkātına nazaran, “muhafızlık” da umûr-ı sâbıka

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before prayer one should prepare in time, make ablution and keep clean, cover the body, face the qibla, use clean clothes and place, attend congregation where possible, and clear the heart of distraction and ostentation.
rows.anchor: abdest ve temizliğe ve setr-i avret, taleb-i kıble, temiz elbise ve temiz yer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During prayer one should understand it as ascent to God and remain attentive in recitation and remembrance without looking around.
rows.anchor: Namazın huzûr-i Hakk’a yükselten bir mi‘râc olduğunu düşünerek ve hikmetine muttali‘olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prayer one should avoid vain matters and sin.
rows.anchor: Namazdan sonra lağviyyâttan ve günaha girmekten sakınmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maintaining prayer also requires a secure Muslim community, public care for right and wrong, and readiness for guard or jihad so external danger does not prevent prayer or make people fear other than God.
rows.anchor: sâlim bir vatan, bir dâr-ı İslâm ve onda emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’l-münker ile âsâyişi gözetecek bir cemaat lüzûmunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This eighth trait connects communal organization, security, government, and military duty to preserving prayer; while the surah is Meccan and no war command had come, it establishes foundations for preparedness.
rows.anchor: bu sekizinci haslet, İslâm’da cemaat kurumuyla âsâyiş, idare ve askerlik işlerinin namazı muhafaza gayesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight virtues are framed by prayer at beginning and end and summed up in the praying believer, showing prayer as religion's pillar; they are like the eight gates of Paradise.
rows.anchor: bu sekiz hasletin evvel ve âhiri namaz işi ile çerçevelenerek hepsi de “musallî” vasfında hulâsa edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to say he invokes and worships only his Creator and Lord; opposition gives no reason for surprise or hostility, and he will not associate anyone with God or hope or fear in another.
rows.anchor: ben ancak Rabbime dua ediyorum ve ederim yani neye öyle üzerime veya aleyhime keçeleniyorsunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning harm alongside guidance rather than benefit uses the rhetorical figure ihtibāk: he independently controls neither harm nor benefit, misguidance nor guidance.
rows.anchor: “Zarar” mukabili “menfaat” zikredilmek iktizâ ederken, “gayy ü dalâl” mukabili olan “rüşd” zikredilmesinde bir nevi ihtibak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those gathering against the Prophet for fear of harm or hope of benefit should know he can do none of these things on his own; God does them, so they should fear and hope in God.
rows.anchor: ben size kendiliğimden bunların hiçbirini yapmaya mâlik değilim, onu Rabbim yapar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet disobeyed God by worshiping another, no human, jinn, angel, or other being could rescue him from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: emrine muhalefet eyleyecek olursam Allah azab eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no refuge apart from God from His majesty or others' hostility; everyone is under His power, so worship and supplication belong to Him alone, as do people's fear and hope.
rows.anchor: O’ndan başka bir sığınacak bulamam gerek O’nun celâlinden ve gerek başkalarının adâvet ve ızrârından sığınacak melce’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One must not conclude before the exception that asking the Prophet for benefit is forbidden; the commentary rejects the Wahhabi claim that seeking his intercession or mediation in prayer is shirk.
rows.anchor: Vehhâbîler duada Peygamber’le tevessülü, “şefaat yâ Resûlallah” demeyi şirk addetmeye kadar gitmişlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception attaches to the Prophet's lack of power to benefit or guide: he is authorized to convey God's message and communications, whether they concern harm or benefit; execution belongs to God.
rows.anchor: Bu istisnâ yukarıki لَآ أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّۭا وَلَا رَشَدًۭا’dan istisnâdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God's communications may parse with God's name in the genitive or as an accusative coordinated with conveyance; the Prophet possesses the duty of conveying as God's messenger.
rows.anchor: وَرِسَٰلَٰتِهِۦ de ya mecrur olarak karîbi olan lafza-i celâleye yahut da kesre ile mansub olarak بَلَٰغًۭا üzerine ma‘tuftur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger's task is conveyance, as 5:99 says; people may seek his prayers as God's envoy, and believers may ask one another for prayer, which brings reassurance.
rows.anchor: kulları tarafından Allah’a risalet ile dua ve niyâza

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This exception grants the Prophet a great rank: though he owns nothing independently, God who sent him owns everything, and love or obedience toward the Prophet is love or obedience toward God.
rows.anchor: O Allah’ın kulu böyle bir resuldür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disobedience to both God and His Messenger leads to eternal Hell; the word abadan signals rebellion involving shirk and disbelief.
rows.anchor: Burada أَبَدًا kaydı isyânın şirk ve küfür ile isyan demek olduğunu anlatır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who call the Prophet and his followers weak and few may persist until they see the promised punishment, when they will know who truly has fewer and weaker helpers.
rows.anchor: Seni ve yardımcını zayıf ve adedinizi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here in is a negation meaning la adri: unless God conveys it, the Prophet does not know whether the promised event is near or whether his Lord gives it a distant term.
rows.anchor: burada اِنْ nâfiyedir. لاَ اَدْرِي demektir. Yani de ki: Rabbimden tebliğ olunmayınca dirayet ile bilmem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen is what is absent from sense, knowledge, or presence; something present to one person may be unseen to another, as a person's heart is hidden from others.
rows.anchor: Birçok şeyler nefsü’l-emrde, vücudda âlem-i şehadette hazır olduğu hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Relative unseen may be known directly or through signs; God knows even what has not yet come into being, and nothing is unseen to Him.
rows.anchor: Haddizâtında mevcud ve hazır olduğu için doğrudan doğru veya delâil ve emârâtından bilinmek şânıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one receives certain, open disclosure of God's absolute unseen knowledge; dreams, inspiration, miracles, or hidden causes may suggest things but do not yield certainty free from doubt.
rows.anchor: bunların hiçbirisi zan ve vehimden ârî tam bir keşf ve izhar mânasına yakīnî bir ilim olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scientific induction and logical inference about future events remain analogical judgments rather than mathematical certainty; appearance and actual disclosure differ.
rows.anchor: vâkı‘ât üzerinde cereyan eden fennî istikrâların, mantıkī istidlâllerin bile yarın için hükmü bir kıyastan ileri geçemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may choose a messenger and disclose some future or unseen matters relevant to the mission, such as miracles, obligations, rulings, and promises; this is conveyed knowledge, not independent unseen knowledge.
rows.anchor: ihtiyar edip dilediği bir resul müstesnâ dilerse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Hour's certainty is revealed, its timing is withheld, as in 46:23 and 67:26.
rows.anchor: kıyametin her hâlde olacağı bildirilmiş ise de yakın mı uzak mı ne zaman olacağı bildirilmemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God places watchers before and behind the messenger to guard revelation from interference by jinn, devils, or other creatures; intruders are struck by shooting flames.
rows.anchor: o resûlün önünden ve arkasından, her tarafından gözetecek birtakım râsıd melekler dizer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn and devils cannot insert anything into the protected revelation; they only try to overhear from afar and use stolen fragments for divination, but are driven off by piercing flames.
rows.anchor: uzaktan uzağa sezer, kulak hırsızlığı kabîlinden bir şey çalmak ve bununla kehanet yapmak için sokulmaya çalışırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shooting-star protection is a miracle specific to Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: bu hâssa risâlet-i Muhammediyeye mahsus olan şihab mucizesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The watchers allow the messenger to know with certainty that God's emissaries delivered His messages faithfully and without hidden alteration.
rows.anchor: o resul şunu bilsin bütün şâhidleriyle mertebe-i şuhûdda yakīnen şuna ilim hâsıl etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompasses all that is with the watchers and messenger and records every thing in full detail and number, so the messenger can perform his duty with certainty.
rows.anchor: gerek o râsıdların ve gerek o resûlün nezdinde olan bitenin hepsini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After three surahs explain the oath in 69:38–39 about what is seen and unseen, and the Prophet's character and revelation in 68:4, al-Muzzammil follows by beginning commands for his mission concerning the visible world.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’in kadr ü hüviyeti ve vahyin sûret-i cereyânı anlatıldıktan sonra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rise for the night except for a little of it; half the night is specified, with a minimum quarter and up to three quarters when increasing the portion.
rows.anchor: yarısından az kalk, amma o eksiltmek yarının yarısından yani gecenin dörtte birinden fazla olmasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The half, subtraction, and increase may describe either the time spent standing or the small excluded remainder, since either complementary calculation gives the same result.
rows.anchor: Gerek müstesnâ minh gerek müstesnâ hangi taraftan mülâhaza edilse netice aynı olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because subtraction and increase address the addressee's action, they describe the duration of standing; following Abu al-Su'ud, half is an explanatory substitute for the excepted portion of the night.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud’un dediği gibi نِّصْفَهُۥٓ zamîrinin râci‘olduğu müstesnâ minh “leyl”den bedel olarak kıyam müddetini beyan olmak zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical wording first follows the usual rule that an exception is smaller, signals that standing more than half is preferable, and treats sleep as little in value compared with worshipful remembrance.
rows.anchor: Bunda başlıca üç nükte vardır. Birincisi; evvelemirde istisnânın az olması kāidesine tenbih

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three possible portions are offered according to circumstances and the changing length of nights; a quarter is the minimum established as obligatory, while more is recommended.
rows.anchor: farz, ziyadesi nedb ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl means arranging something well and clearly, without flaw, and fully delivering what is due; distinct, well-ordered teeth and measured, composed speech illustrate the term.
rows.anchor: “Tertîl” bir şeyi güzel tensik ve tertib ile kusursuz olarak açık açık hakkını îfâ ederek tebyin eylemektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic tartīl gives every letter, pronunciation, arrangement, and meaning its full due; the emphatic verbal noun tartīlan demands the finest degree of recitation.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın tertîli de böyle her harfinin, edâsının, nazmının, mânasının hakkını doyura doyura vererek okunmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A beautiful text loses its beauty when badly recited, and readers who cannot recite well can ruin good words.
rows.anchor: Bir söz haddizâtında ne kadar güzel olursa olsun gereği gibi güzel okunmayınca güzelliği kalmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl is not arbitrary singing that stretches and bends sounds like a string instrument; it requires tajwīd guided by meaning, eloquence, and spiritual fit.
rows.anchor: sade ses güzelliğiyle gelişigüzel eze büze tegannî etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajwīd varies force and softness, length and shortening, nasalization and clear pronunciation, concealment and assimilation, connection and pause, to understand and convey the meaning.
rows.anchor: bütün maksad mânayı duymak ve mümkin olduğu kadar duyurmak olmak üzere tecvid ile okumak işidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajwīd is necessary, but perfecting articulation by cracking the qāf must not obscure the meaning.
rows.anchor: Tecvid de kaf çatlatmak derdiyle çatlatmaktaki mânayı gayb etmek değildir
